authority_bypass_risks.answer: Yes at the current-main application boundary; no evidence that the release accepts browser-supplied tenant or authority claims.
authority_bypass_risks.browser_claim_layer: The release handler extracts only Bearer authorization or the openclaw_session cookie and the Stage-2 server context rejects client authority fields. The unauthenticated POST probes returned 401.
authority_bypass_risks.main_authority_layer: The live process uses release hashes for server_cli.py and http_api.py that differ from current main. It runs isolated Stage2ServerApp and release-specific HTTP handlers rather than current main AccountAuthService, WorkspaceResolver, SessionPrincipal and current HTTP authority composition.
authority_bypass_risks.canonical_data_layer: The release production factory directly reads canonical account, tenant, membership, Stage-1 binding and source tables through its own SQL readers, including a session-token and CSRF hash check. This is a server-side check but is a duplicated authority adapter, not proof that current main authority semantics are used.
risks: Authentication, tenant selection, membership, binding generation and status semantics can drift from current main.
The release entrypoint and HTTP surface can diverge from current main API middleware, error mapping, audit and authorization behavior.
The release route is exposed through a separate 8443 to 8892 deployment boundary and is not the current main 8787 server surface.
An authenticated request would update session last-seen state and could write personal or Feishu artifacts; those paths were not exercised in this read-only review.

required_main_changes: Add POST /stage2/personal and POST /stage2/organization to the current main HTTP authority/dispatch path without replacing current main app.py, adapters/http_api.py or server_cli.py with the older release copies.

Compose the Stage2Gateway in the current main startup owner, or add a narrow current-main adapter, while preserving AccountAuthService, WorkspaceResolver, SessionPrincipal, tenant authorization and current error/audit behavior.

Use current-main authority adapters for session, tenant, workspace, active Binding, profile and source resolution; remove the release-only duplicate SQL authority path or prove and enforce one shared implementation.

Only after that wiring is present, promote the writer contract status to accepted, runtimeIntegration to true and add the two endpoints, with a startup digest gate bound to the exact contract used by the current-main process.

Keep the factory fail-closed pair invariant. If list-only targets are needed, implement explicit normalization for complete global-pair-or-complete-list semantics and reject one-sided global configuration rather than deleting the guard.

tests: Update the contract expectation only with the integration change: accepted status, runtimeIntegration true and the two endpoint identities.
Verify startup rejects provisional, endpoint-missing, digest-mismatched and contract-mutated inputs.
Preserve authority-pair, browser-forbidden-field and publishability invariants.
Unauthenticated and malformed Authorization requests return the current stable 401 errors.
Bearer and session-cookie requests resolve through current main account authority and do not accept tenant, workspace, Binding, source or capability overrides from the body.
Personal and organization routes enforce internal and lark authority pairs, respectively, including cross-tenant and stale-Binding negative cases.
Existing media-web routes and current main auth/account/admin behavior remain unchanged.
Accept a complete global space/parent pair.
Accept list-only configuration with complete per-entry pairs and both global values absent.
Reject exactly one global value even when a list entry is present.
Reject incomplete list entries and reject no usable target.
Verify the current Binding target must contain both space and parent before an organization write.
Run authenticated personal and organization E2E against the current-main release, including cross-tenant negatives and idempotent replay.
Verify deployed contract and source hashes, Nginx routing, authenticated DOM or API behavior, actual Feishu write/readback and recovery evidence as separate evidence layers.
Do not convert fixture, unit, status-only or deployment-readback passes into production acceptance.
